sourceText: At the end of each reading-room shift, the volunteer should count returned audio players, check that each is in its numbered sleeve, and enter the count in the green ledger beside the date. If a player is missing, note its number and the time it was last seen, then tell the desk lead before leaving; do not mark the equipment check as complete. The cabinet key stays on the red hook behind the desk, and the charging plugs are kept in the shallow drawer underneath the printer. The room is usually quiet after six, although the poetry group sometimes runs over and may need the chairs left out for a few minutes. On wet evenings, visitors often leave umbrellas near the entrance, so keep the clear walkway open. The ledger is collected on the first Monday of each month by the facilities officer. One exception applies to the inventory entry: if a player is missing during a shift when the desk lead is absent, the volunteer must write “pending lead review” in the ledger and notify the building manager before locking up; the manager is covering only until the lead returns, and should not be asked to authorise disposal or replacement. When all devices are present, the volunteer may initial the check after recording the count. Never take a player home to charge it, even if its battery is empty. The next shift begins at 9 am, and the room should be left unlocked for the cleaner until 8 pm.
objective: Turn the source into a concise handover note of no more than 65 words for the evening archive volunteer. The source is authoritative. Preserve the ordinary process and the distant exception; omit background that does not affect what the volunteer should do. Summarise only equipment inventory and missing-player escalation, including when a check may be initialled. Exclude storage, charging, room-closing and visitor-management instructions.
